offices.does: Decide what to buy and sell, and create the trade

offices.who: Trade operations, pricing and reconciliation analysts
offices.does: Book trades, value every holding, and check our records against the custodian
Keep the official books and calculate the NAV (price per fund share)

outside.gives: Its own record of what each account holds (comparison_positions)
A daily price for every security (prices)
Daily currency rates to US dollars (fx_rates)

reader: Outside sources are not offices: the custodian, the price vendors and the FX provider send us data, and we check it.

stages.office: Front office (set up), back office (fund mapping)
stages.exit: Every account has its required fields, valid open/close dates, and a fund and share class
Every security exists once, has valid codes and currency, and is set up before anyone trades it

stages.office: Front office creates, middle office books
stages.exit: Every trade is unique, valid and on time; every corporate action is complete before its ex-date
Every holding equals its trades, matches the custodian, and has a fresh price
Every fund NAV adds up and has no serious open problem feeding it

handoffs.what: Every trade must belong to a known, open account
Every trade and corporate action must use a known security
Booked trades, on time, add up to each holding
Events like splits and spin-offs adjust every holder correctly
The custodian confirms quantities; vendors give prices and FX rates
Valued holdings roll up into each fund and share class

checks.tests: The account exists, is open on the trade date, and has a fund and share class
checks.fail: Hold the trade and send it to onboarding

checks.tests: The security exists in the security list, and the trade's code and currency match it
checks.fail: Hold the trade until the security is set up

checks.tests: No duplicate trades; required fields filled; dates readable; settles 0 to 2 business days after the trade unless an extension is agreed; booked before cutoff
Before the ex-date: the event's terms are complete for its type, and any new security is already set up
Each holding equals the sum of its trades and matches the custodian; every difference is explained and aged
checks.fail: Flag a break and work it

checks.tests: Every holding has a price from today; the three vendors agree within 0.5%; one valid FX rate per currency, USD = 1
checks.fail: Use the next vendor, or flag

checks.tests: Net assets / shares = NAV per share; every account maps to a fund; no serious open break or price issue feeds the fund

defects.example: A trade uses a security that is not in the security list
defects.evidence: Security list vs the IDs used in trades and corporate actions
defects.missed: Trades cannot be priced; every holder of that security is wrong at once

defects.example: The same trade is booked twice
defects.evidence: Same trade ID twice, or same account, security, date, quantity and price
defects.missed: Holding overstated, so value and NAV overstated

defects.example: A trade misses the cutoff or has impossible dates
defects.evidence: Timestamps vs cutoff; trade and settlement dates
defects.missed: Today's NAV misses the trade; settlement goes wrong
defects.data: 1,124 settle before trade date; 1,687 unreadable dates

defects.example: A spin-off reaches some holders but not others
defects.evidence: Event terms, new security set up, list of holders
defects.missed: Some accounts right, others wrong; new shares cannot be priced
defects.data: All 23 spin-off targets missing from the security list

defects.defect: Positions that don't match their history
defects.example: Our book says 2,028, the trades add up to 1,900
defects.evidence: Rebuild from trades vs our book vs the custodian
defects.missed: PM trades on wrong holdings; NAV built on wrong quantities

defects.evidence: Price age, spread between vendors, FX rates
defects.missed: Wrong value goes straight into the NAV
defects.data: USD rate never exactly 1 in 30 days

defects.evidence: Required fields, open and close dates vs trade dates
defects.missed: Holdings cannot be assigned to a fund, so they are missing from NAV

defects.example: Net assets / shares is not the published NAV
defects.evidence: Net assets, shares outstanding, NAV per share
defects.missed: Investors buy and sell at a wrong price

kpis.kpi: Trades with a valid account and security
kpis.formula: 100 x trades whose account is open and whose security exists / all trades
kpis.decision: Hold failing trades and fix the account or security first

kpis.formula: 100 x trades published by cutoff / trades with readable timestamps
kpis.decision: Escalate a trade feed that misses cutoff two days in a row
Stop and fix the feed that sends duplicates

kpis.formula: 100 x holdings where our book = custodian / holdings in both records
kpis.decision: Staff the break queue; escalate breaks older than 3 days

kpis.kpi: Holdings with a fresh, agreed price
kpis.formula: 100 x held securities priced today with vendors within 0.5% / held securities
kpis.decision: Challenge vendors before the NAV is struck

kpis.formula: 100 x fund rows where net assets / shares = NAV / all fund rows
kpis.decision: Hold publication of any NAV that fails

kpis.kpi: Funds released with no serious open issue
kpis.formula: 100 x funds whose NAV had no open break or price issue above threshold / funds
kpis.decision: Hold or caveat the NAV of a fund with open issues

excluded_dimensions: Precision and accessibility are not scored: precision is handled by stated tolerances inside the checks (e.g. 0.5% vendor spread), and accessibility cannot be measured from a static data extract.

promises.promise: Every trade's account exists, is open on the trade date, and has a fund and share class
promises.kpi: Trades with a valid account and security

promises.promise: Every security on a trade or corporate action exists once in the security list, with the same code and currency
promises.kpi: Trades with a valid account and security

promises.promise: Every trade is unique, complete, has readable dates, settles 0 to 2 business days later (unless agreed) and is booked before cutoff
promises.breach: Any failing trade; a feed is in breach above 0.5% of a batch
promises.kpi: Duplicate trade rate; trades booked before cutoff

promises.promise: Each event has complete terms for its type, a written meaning for each date, and any new security set up at least 2 business days before the ex-date
The custodian sends one record per account and security each day; every held security has a price from today; one FX rate per currency per day, USD = 1
promises.breach: Any missing record, price or rate
promises.kpi: Positions matching the custodian; holdings with a fresh, agreed price

promises.promise: Each fund and share class has one NAV row per day where net assets / shares = NAV, and no serious open break feeds it
promises.kpi: NAV rows that add up; funds released with no serious open issue

missing.what: A log of which accounts received each corporate action
missing.why: We can check an event was set up correctly, but not that it reached every holder

missing.what: The custodian's confirmation that a trade actually settled
missing.why: settlement_date is only the planned date

missing.what: Cash, fees and accruals per fund
missing.why: We cannot rebuild a fund's net assets from its holdings

missing.what: A clear 'type of change' on each trade (new, cancel, reversal)
missing.why: A REVERSED trade could mean two different things

operating_model.a: The corporate actions lead owns it, because it entered when the spin-off was set up. The security master lead creates the missing security; fund accounting is told for every affected fund.
Rank open problems by: will it reach a NAV, then how many accounts and funds, then how much money is exposed, then how cheap the fix is. This one is top priority: it already sits in held positions.
Both: set up the missing security and correct the affected holdings, and change the event intake so an incomplete event is quarantined, or it happens again.
Run the corporate action check at least 2 business days before the ex-date, with an automatic request to set up any new security. About 200 events a month: cheap to run.
One ticket per problem with owner, age and exposure, shown on the overall scorecard. Anything open past 2 business days is escalated to management; fund accounting holds or caveats an affected NAV.

scores: Scores are produced daily after cutoff with one command and read by each owner every morning. A disputed score is re-run from the written rules with evidence; scores are never edited by hand.

maturity.text: Problems found after the fact, office by office, in spreadsheets; nobody owns them
Written checks with owners and targets at every handoff, a daily scorecard, problems ticketed
Checks sit at the earliest stage and stop bad data before it moves; tested with injected errors

rollup: The platform data quality score rolls up from the rules and domains of the scorecard, always shown next to its coverage (the share of records we could actually test). The 7 KPIs are the office view beside it, each with its own value and target.
